newsitem.title: CHILE: Escondida says strike will not hurt copper output.
newsitem.headline: Escondida says strike will not hurt copper output.

text.p: Chile's largest copper mine Escondida said its production will not be hurt by a strike agreed Tuesday by a small group of unionized workers representing 17 percent of the pit's workforce.
"Minera Escondida will not suffer an alteration in its operations," said the statement released Wednesday.
"The company will guarantee, through all the means granted by the law, the security and freedom to work to the large majority of workers who did not take part in this process."
Union officials said 206 workers out of 353 union members involved in the collective negotiations voted to strike from 0800 local (1300 GMT) Friday.
The rest of the mine's 2,000 strong workforce did not vote and are unlikely to take part in the strike, they said.
Escondida, the world's largest copper pit, is owned by Broken Hill Proprietary and RTZ Corp Plc. It produced over 800,000 tonnes of the red metal last year.
